title: The Data science mode redrawn as the Claude desktop app beside the untouched Developer mode, with the notebook as DCLab Studio's review in Claude's colours
request: The owner: keep DCLab's UI as the Developer mode as it is now, and add a Data science mode with the same functionality but very similar to Claude Code, more data-science friendly, with a switch between them; the first attempt was a mistake (the result was the same page recoloured). With screenshots of their dclab code app, DCLab Studio's notebook review and the Claude desktop app; answers: both looks combined, every page at once, Claude's colours; then: I really like Claude's style more, beside the old one; and for the notebook DCLab Studio's style in Claude's theme and colours.
spec: One set of pages, two frames: html[data-mode=ds] draws the Claude desktop app's frame (New chat, Recents of drafts and projects, the pages folded under Pages, account and Settings at the foot; back and forward, DCLab / page, search, the side panel's toggle, Settings), Home as a new session (What are we working on?, one box with its chips) then the conversation with your words in bubbles and the context in a side panel, every shared part in Claude's calm style, the notebook as DCLab Studio's review; Developer never changes; Settings holds only switches the product has.
plan: Screenshot the first attempt beside Developer to see the mistake
Ask which screenshot, how much and which colours before building
Read the shell, Home's composer and messages, the notebook's cells and findings, the list endpoints
Add the frame's parts to the shell (Data science only) and dsFrame in core.js calling the product's own functions
Rewrite ds.css on the kept Claude tokens: frame, every page, Home, conversation, side panel, notebook, Settings, command list
Screenshot light, dark and 375 px; extend the browser check; run the browser checks, the web tests and rd-gates

decisions.decision: Same pages, a second frame: no page copied for Data science
decisions.why: the owner asked for the same functionality; 930 KB of pages copied would drift from Developer and break

decisions.decision: Settings shows only switches the product has (look, theme, view as, pages, blueprint, tours); models and budgets point to Admin
decisions.why: the dclab code screenshot showed model, effort and cap pickers the studio's Home does not have; drawing them would be controls that do nothing

decisions.decision: No Review gate card on the notebook
decisions.why: DCLab Studio's numbered fix order has no source in the product's review yet; the companion's severity counts sit there instead of an invented order

decisions.decision: Recents reopens a conversation the way Admin's Sessions does (state.resumeDraft, then Home)
decisions.why: one path to reopen a draft, already tested

decisions.decision: The side panel shows in a conversation unless closed; its toggle reads what is on screen
decisions.why: Claude shows its panel in a session and not on a new one; a toggle that only read the saved choice opened an already open panel

decisions.decision: Controls that move keep their action: New project from chat becomes the sidebar's New chat, the start box's Connect data becomes the chat's own; nothing is removed
decisions.why: the owner: all things must work the same; a comparison of every visible control found 3 real gaps and these 2 moves

decisions.decision: The side panel is one session card with the facts of a job or of the lead agent's case file; nothing is invented
decisions.why: the owner asked for the dclab code Jobs panel, which has meters and steps; the product has them for an intern job and a case file for the lead agent, and a part with no facts is left out rather than drawn empty or made up

change: dclab_rnd/agentic/web/src/shell.html (Recents, Pages toggle, account, back/forward, DCLab crumb, side panel and Settings buttons, the Settings window); src/core.js (dsFrame: recents, settings, theme, pages, side panel; Commands first in the palette); src/ds.css (rewritten on the kept tokens); src/views/home.html (What are we working on?); scripts/browser_e2e.py (dsmode extended); tests/test_web_client.py (dsmode in the checks' list); CLAUDE.md; dclab_rnd/agentic/static/app (make web)

findings.defect: The first Data science mode was the Developer page recoloured
findings.scenario: the owner switches to Data science and sees the same Home, tabs, cards and navigation in cream and orange, nothing like Claude Code
findings.cause: it changed tokens and moved Home's cards to a column, but kept the frame (workspace card, big search, role picker) and every page's structure
findings.fix: a Claude desktop frame of its own, Home as a new session, the conversation in bubbles with a side panel, Studio's notebook review
findings.test: scripts/browser_e2e.py check_ds_mode

findings.defect: The sidebar's Recents, Pages and Workspace labels overlapped
findings.scenario: Data science at 1440 x 900: the three headings drawn on top of each other
findings.cause: the sidebar is a scrolling flex column and its new sections shrank to zero height
findings.fix: the sidebar's children never shrink in Data science
findings.test: screenshot at 1440 px; scripts/browser_e2e.py check_ds_mode clicks Pages and Recents

findings.defect: The side panel's toggle opened a panel already open
findings.scenario: in a conversation the panel shows; the first click on its toggle left it showing
findings.cause: the toggle read the saved choice, empty in a first visit, not the panel on screen
findings.fix: the toggle reads the panel's display and sets the other way
findings.test: scripts/browser_e2e.py check_ds_mode: the side panel closes and opens

findings.defect: The list of browser checks a test expects did not name dsmode
findings.scenario: tests/test_web_client.py failed on the committed code: the first Data science commit added the check, not the list
findings.cause: the check was added without its test's list
findings.fix: dsmode named in the list
findings.test: tests/test_web_client.py test_the_browser_tests_visit_every_page_the_app_has

findings.defect: The logo's letters were unreadable in the dark theme
findings.scenario: Data science, dark: white DC on the light clay square
findings.cause: the mark's text kept the light theme's white
findings.fix: the mark's text uses the brand's own on-colour
findings.test: screenshot in the dark theme

findings.defect: The project switcher on project pages was a blank white button
findings.scenario: Data science, the notebook page: the 'Project: Churn' chip drawn white text on white
findings.cause: the general white-button rule replaced its green ground while its text stayed white
findings.fix: the switcher drawn as a quiet chip with dark text
findings.test: screenshot of the notebook page

findings.defect: The top bar scrolled away and text showed above the sticky tabs
findings.scenario: a long page scrolled down: no top bar, the page's text visible in the gap above the tabs
findings.cause: the top bar is static (in Developer too) while the tabs stick below its height
findings.fix: in Data science the top bar is pinned, as Claude's; Developer unchanged
findings.test: screenshot of the notebook scrolled

findings.defect: A new conversation did not appear in Recents until a page change

findings.cause: Recents refreshed only on a page change or a project change
findings.fix: Recents refreshes when Home's conversation opens
findings.test: scripts/browser_e2e.py check_ds_mode on a fresh workspace

findings.defect: The clean version's cells touched their card's edge
findings.scenario: Notebook, Clean version: the file name and cells flush with the card's border
findings.cause: the toolbar and cells lost their padding with the overview's flat column
findings.fix: padding inside the cards of the other tabs
findings.test: screenshot of the Clean version tab

findings.defect: Nothing showed that Data science does everything Developer does
findings.scenario: the owner: all things must work the same; only the notebook and Home had been checked by eye in the new look
findings.cause: the browser suite ran only in Developer; the Data science check covered pages loading, not actions
findings.fix: scripts/browser_e2e.py takes --mode ds and runs all 15 checks (chat, build, five stages, brief, decisions, team, memory, review, failures, 375 px) in the new look; a control-by-control comparison of 1,800 controls on every page and tab found the gaps below
findings.test: scripts/browser_e2e.py --mode ds

findings.defect: The project switcher was gone from Home in Data science

findings.fix: the row stays with the switcher and the New project link; only the New project from chat button steps aside, the sidebar's New chat runs the same action
findings.test: scripts/browser_e2e.py checks decide, switch, memory, review in --mode ds

findings.defect: What needs the person was hidden on Home's start page
findings.scenario: a draft waits for an answer (Needs you: 1); in Data science the start page showed no sign of it unless the side panel was opened
findings.cause: the side panel showed only in a conversation or when opened
findings.fix: the panel opens by default when Needs you has items, unless the person closed it

findings.defect: Home's Overview, Projects and Activity tabs were hidden beside an open conversation

findings.fix: the tabs stay, with the conversation first
findings.test: control comparison with a chat open

findings.defect: The conversation sat below the workflow drawing, its title behind the reply box

findings.cause: the card precedes the chat in the page and the reply box is pinned
findings.fix: in Data science the conversation comes first and the card follows (order only)

findings.defect: The browser checks clicked controls that move in the new look
findings.scenario: flow clicked the start box's Connect data and Home's New project from chat; in Data science the chat has its own Connect data and the sidebar has New chat
findings.cause: the checks named one place for each control
findings.fix: the checks click whichever of the two is on screen (both run the same action)
findings.test: scripts/browser_e2e.py connect_data, new_chat_button

findings.defect: Under the lead agent the person's own messages never showed in the chat
findings.scenario: a person answers the agent's question; the chat shows only the agent's replies, and the buttons of the question they answered stay live (the owner's screenshot: no user prompt in the chat)
findings.cause: the lead agent's Home saved the person's message to the draft but did not send it to the page; the page draws the chat only from what is sent, so it never showed, even after a reload. The rules-first Home saves and sends. This held in Developer too, since 37.9
findings.fix: CaseHome._hear saves and sends it as the rules-first Home does, on all four paths (an ordinary reply, a pick, a build answer, a column check)
findings.test: tests/test_case_home.py test_the_persons_words_are_sent_to_the_page_on_every_path_under_the_lead_agent, test_a_pick_of_an_option_is_sent_to_the_page_too

findings.defect: The person's first sentence was nowhere in the chat in Data science
findings.scenario: a chat opens: the start box that held the sentence steps aside and no bubble holds it
findings.cause: the page never drew the problem sentence as a message (Developer keeps it in the start box)
findings.fix: Data science draws it as the first bubble from the draft's problem; Developer hides that bubble
findings.test: scripts/browser_e2e.py check_ds_mode: the first bubble

findings.defect: The lead agent's Home left the Solution workflow card empty, and shown on a segment report
findings.scenario: the person asks for a segment report: the agent starts an analysis and the page shows an empty Solution workflow card with blank tags, as the owner's screenshot shows
findings.cause: the page learns the workflow and the route only from sent events; the lead agent's Home sent neither, and the page shows the card by default
findings.fix: a prediction route draws the workflow once (sent as the rules-first Home sends it); the page shows the card only when the lead agent's route is a prediction
findings.test: tests/test_case_home.py test_a_prediction_route_draws_the_workflow_once_and_other_routes_draw_none; a scripted lead agent run on the real server

findings.fix: the workflow card joins the side panel; Data science shows the same blocks as compact tiles by state, the gates and revisits as lines, a tile opens its block as a click on the drawing does; Developer keeps the drawing
findings.test: scripts/browser_e2e.py check_ds_mode: ten tiles in the panel, beside the chat, a tile opens its block, Developer keeps its drawing

findings.defect: An empty tag was drawn beside the workflow's version
findings.scenario: the card's pack name is blank under the lead agent: an empty pill
findings.cause: the pack tag is filled only when a pack is read
findings.fix: an empty tag is not drawn in Data science
findings.test: screenshot of a prediction chat

findings.defect: The Data science side panel was a stack of Developer's cards, not a session panel
findings.scenario: the owner attaches the dclab code app's Jobs panel: one card for the task with its status, a Plan row, tool-call and minute meters, ten workflow tiles in a row of five and a list of steps; the panel showed the workflow tiles in two columns under several cards
findings.cause: the first panel moved Developer's context cards to a column and only restyled them
findings.fix: one session card built from real data: an intern job's status, plan, budget, tokens, project graph and every tool call (the data the intern page shows), or the lead agent's case file (its recorded moves, its spend against the cap) with the draft's workflow tiles; polled while a job works; a part with no facts is not drawn
findings.test: scripts/browser_e2e.py check_ds_mode: the card names the task, ten tiles, beside the chat; checked on a real standard-plan intern job and a scripted lead agent

findings.defect: A tool call showed raw data instead of a phrase

findings.fix: the intern page's phrases for both
findings.test: a real intern job on the page

measurements.name: browser checks on a local server (no model): dsmode, pages, mobile, ui, flow
measurements.gate: all pass; Developer unchanged at 1150 to 1366 px; 21 pages without an error and within 375 px in Data science
measurements.result: all pass; Developer's Home screenshot identical to before the change
limits: headless Chromium in a cloud sandbox, not the owner's Mac browsers
a fresh workspace with one built project and a few drafts

measurements.name: the complete browser suite in Data science (15 checks), and a control-by-control comparison with Developer (about 1,800 controls on 21 pages and their tabs)
measurements.gate: every check passes in both looks; every Developer control is on screen in Data science or has its stated place
measurements.result: 14 of 15 pass in Data science; poll fails in both looks on some runs (a timing flake in this sandbox, also failing in the Developer baseline); the comparison found 3 gaps (switcher, Needs you, Home tabs) and 2 moved controls, all fixed or placed
limits: headless Chromium in a cloud sandbox
the comparison sees what is visible, not what is correct: the browser checks cover actions
a control that only shows after a rare event (an error, a long job) was not compared

outcome: Data science is now its own Claude-style frame over the same pages, with Home as a session and conversation, a side panel, Settings and Commands, every page in Claude's style and the notebook as DCLab Studio's review; Developer is unchanged.
lessons: Before redoing a design that missed, screenshot it beside its target and ask which target, how much and which colours
A second look over the same pages keeps the functionality the same; a copied page would not
Draw only controls the product has: a picker that does nothing is worse than none
Run the browser check on a fresh workspace too: lists that already had items hid that a new item never appeared
To show two looks do the same, run the same suite in both and compare every control: the eye found the notebook, the comparison found the missing project switcher

When the owner shows a screenshot, find the cause in the layer that decides what the page learns (the events the server sends), not only in the look: two of the three gaps were in the server and hit Developer too
The page draws only what is sent: a new agent for Home must send every event the older one sends (message, status, workflow), checked by a test of the events, not of the saved draft

When the owner attaches the other app's panel, find what the product already records for the same things (here the intern's steps, budget and tokens) before drawing it: the card then shows the same facts and nothing is made up
risks: Pages other than Home and the notebook are restyled, not re-laid-out: they read calmer but keep Developer's arrangement
The look relies on :has(), supported by current Chrome, Safari and Firefox, not by old browsers
Recents lists at most 14 items and refreshes on a page change at most every 15 seconds
